newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia palm oil futures volume falls in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia palm oil futures volume falls in 1996.

text.p: Trading volume in the crude palm oil futures contract on the Kuala Lumpur Commodity Exchange declined in 1996, Bank Negara Malaysia said in its annual report released on Friday.
The volume dropped to 498,118 lots, or 12.5 million tonnes of crude palm oil in 1996, from 525,889 lots in 1995.
Average daily turnover in 1996 was 2,004 lots or 50,098 tonnes, against 2,160 lots or 53,996 tonnes in 1995, it said.
The central bank said the fall was due to the less volatile movement in crude palm oil prices during the year.
Total open positions declined to 9,897 lots at the end of 1996, compared with 10,468 lots a year earlier.

During the year, the average futures price declined sharply by 20 percent to 1,175 ringgit per tonne against 1,466 ringgit in 1995. This was due to higher palm oil production in Malaysia and lower exports to major consuming countries, the Bank said.
